title: On Clarifying the last point before voting
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：clarify　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 clarify 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the guide ① clarified the last point before voting before dawn, and every traveller in the valley said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the guide ② clarifies the last point before voting in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ clarify the last point before voting at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ clarified the last point before voting before — a line in the guidebook for July 1970 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Clarifying the last point before voting before dawn, the guide said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ clarify the difference between the two plans in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Clarify the difference between the two plans at once and never mention it again.

By 1983 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook, and a new traveller from the next valley ⑧ clarifies the difference between the two plans before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ledge, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ clarified the last point before voting again when nobody else would.

⑩ To clarify the last point before voting, my mother said in 1988, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the valley remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the valley forgets, somebody clarifies the last point before voting in public again and somebody must clarify the last point before voting before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 澄清（一般过去式 clarified the last point before voting：1976 年向导头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 澄清（一般现在 clarifies the last point before voting：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 澄清（不定式 to clarify the last point before voting：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 澄清（过去完成时 had clarified the last point before voting：1970 年七月的旅行手册上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 澄清（动名词 clarifying the last point before voting 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 讲清楚（clarify the difference between the two plans：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去讲清楚把两套方案的差别说清）
G. v. 讲清楚（clarify the difference between the two plans：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 澄清（后段两处：新来的旅人照例 clarifies the difference between the two plans，而母亲又一次 clarified the last point before voting）

answers.why: clarify 意为“澄清”，1976 年向导天没亮就澄清表决前把最后一点讲清，那是山谷里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 clarified。
clarify 意为“澄清”，自那以后向导当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 clarifies。
clarify 意为“澄清”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯澄清表决前把最后一点讲清”，此处为不定式 to clarify the last point before voting。
clarify 意为“澄清”，旅行手册里 七月 那行字说明早在 1983 年之前就有人澄清过，故用过去完成时 had clarified。
clarify 意为“澄清”，向导说“澄清表决前把最后一点讲清这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 clarifying the last point before voting 作主语。
clarify 意为“讲清楚”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去讲清楚把两套方案的差别说清”，should ever 之后用原形 clarify the difference between the two plans。
clarify 意为“讲清楚”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻讲清楚把两套方案的差别说清（clarify the difference between the two plans at once），以后再也不要提起。
clarify 意为“澄清”，新来的旅人每个日子都照例讲清楚把两套方案的差别说清，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 clarifies。
clarify 意为“澄清”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就澄清表决前把最后一点讲清，用一般过去式 clarified 叙述。
clarify 意为“澄清”，结尾那句是母亲 1988 年的话：要澄清表决前把最后一点讲清，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和山谷记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 clarify 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1976 the guide clarified the last point before voting before dawn, and nobody in the valley forgot it.
Even now the guide clarifies the last point before voting in public whenever the valley asks.
Clarifying the last point before voting before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever clarify the difference between the two plans in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next valley clarifies the difference between the two plans before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother clarified the last point before voting again, and the valley remembered that half.
